children: Sri Lanka’s Services PMI rose to 65.6 in August 2026 from 61.4 in July, marking the highest level since December of 2025 and expanding for a fourth consecutive month.
Growth was supported by stronger performance across sectors, primarily in transportation, wholesale and retail trade, and professional services.
This was also reflected in assessments of new business, which increased, albeit at a slightly slower pace than in the previous month.
Employment rose, supported by new recruitment, while backlogs of work declined.
Looking ahead, firms remained optimistic, supported by expectations of higher tourist arrivals.
However, sentiment weakened as broader economic uncertainty continued to pose downside risks.

title: Sri Lanka Services Growth Hits Highest Since December
